Subject: Temporary cross-zone extract for analytics — scope + subprocessors

Hi Hannah / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have a short follow-up from our compliance and analytics teams: for an upcoming analytics sprint (2 weeks), we need to run a controlled extract of de-identified prompts and embeddings to a partner analytics cluster hosted in the US.

Key asks:
- Can Redwood confirm whether that processing would require a formal DPA addendum for temporary cross-border processing?
- Do you have a short list of subprocessors that would be involved in the extract path (edge caches, analytics infra, monitoring)?
- What controls exist to limit the window (we need strict 72-hour maximum storage in the US) and proof of deletion?

I've attached our current subprocessor matrix and a redline from Legal Ops.

[Attachment: subprocessor_roster_202704.pdf (PDF, 58KB)]

Appreciate a quick runbook /template we can use for approvals — our SOC2 and DPO teams will review. We aim to start the extract on Tue 20 Apr.

Best,
Sophie

Subject: Re: Temporary cross-zone extract for analytics — scope + subprocessors

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear asks. Quick answers and proposed next steps below.

Short answers:
- DPA addendum: yes, for a timebound cross-border extract we recommend a one-page DPA addendum that enumerates the exact scope, retention window (72h), permitted actions, and audit evidence expectations.
- Subprocessors: primary candidates are (1) Redwood edge cache (for transient routing), (2) Analytics ingestion partner (US), and (3) observability vendor for telemetry. I'll attach our standard subprocessor roster summary.
- Controls & proof: we can provide a deletion certificate (ops audit) plus a short telemetry snapshot showing no reads after deletion. We can also implement a scoped KMS key usage with explicit TTL for the extract artifact.

Proposed runbook (high level):
1) Legal sign-off on one-page addendum (I can circulate draft by EOD).
2) Ops scheduling: confirm start/end timestamps and the exact data set hash.
3) KMS escrow toggle: use customer-scoped key or escrowed key per your preference — Karthik, can you confirm feasibility for a 72h TTL key?
4) Proof & evidence: deletion cert + telemetry export + subprocessor audit note delivered within 5 business days.

Marissa / Karthik / Soojin — any technical constraints or objections to an April 20–22 window? If Karithik can confirm the KMS TTL we'll prepare the addendum draft and a minimal Ops checklist for sign-off.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Ops notes — temporary extract path
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Karthik / Soojin — following Hannah's proposal, quick ops considerations:

- Data selection: we will accept a hash manifest (list of IDs) to strictly scoping records to extract. No full exports via bulk queries.
- Transit path: EU region -> short-hop edge -> US ingestion endpoint. Edge cache retention will be disabled for this job (cache bypass flag).
- Temporary artifact storage: encrypted object in a customer-scoped S3 bucket with lifecycle delete after 72 hours. We will emit a deletion event to an audit log.
- KMS: we can support a TTL-wrapped key if customer provides a KMS key ARN. If customer prefers Redwood-managed key, we can set a 72h TTL wrapper but will need Legal approval for escrow exceptions.

Risks / gaps:
- Observability vendor currently retains 7 days by default; we can request a scoped retention reduction but need vendor sign-off (Soojin, pls confirm if we have a special SLA for MedSys).
- Subprocessor evidence: some vendors only provide monthly attestation. Will need to note that in the addendum.

Action items:
- Karthik: confirm TTL KMS pattern and whether we can produce a deletion certificate automatically.
- Soojin: check observability vendor retention exception timeline.
- Hannah: circulate the one-page addendum to Sophie and Legal Ops once KMS approach is confirmed.

Marissa
VP, Product Compliance — Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah / Marissa — this is helpful. A few follow-ups before we sign the addendum: 

- Can you confirm that the deletion certificate includes an S3 object digest and timestamp? We need that for our audit.
- For KMS: MedSys prefers to supply the KMS key ARN (we run keys in our cloud). If Redwood can accommodate that and confirm no key material leaves our account, Legal will be comfortable.
- Observability retention: if your vendor requires >72h, can Redwood provide a scoped export limited to our job (so we still get telemetry without long-term retention)?

If you can confirm the points above in writing, I'll route the addendum to Legal Ops and get back with a DocuSign link. Proposed window still Apr 20–22 (UTC conversion noted).
